post.caption:
Roman aqueducts held consistent gradients of a few centimetres per kilometre across enormous distances. Too flat and the channel silts up, too steep and the water scours the stone out. Where a valley was too deep to bridge, inverted siphons carried the water down one side and back up the other under pressure. No pumps anywhere in the system. The arches are the photogenic part. The surveying is the actual achievement.
